stem.en: A ball of mass 2 kg is thrown straight up at 20 m/s. It reaches a height of 19.4 m. Take g = 10 m/s^2. How much work does air resistance do on the ball on the way up, in joules? Give the sign.

explanation.en: Kinetic energy at the start: 1/2 x 2 x 20^2 = 400 J. Potential energy at the top: 2 x 10 x 19.4 = 388 J. The missing 12 J was taken by air resistance, which pushes against the motion. So air resistance did -12 J of work on the ball.

hints.en: Compare the kinetic energy at the start with the potential energy at the top.
Air resistance acts against the motion, so its work is negative.
